NRES 100.title: Pursuing Innovative Solutions to Big Questions
NRES 100.description: Multidisciplinary approaches to solving pressing challenges in natural resources. Diversifying perspectives of natural resources and land stewardship. Skill-building in written and verbal communication, collaboration, and critical thinking. This course includes a field trip. Fees will be assessed to meet expenses.

NRES 103.title: Pathways in Natural Resources
NRES 103.description: Exploration of disciplines within natural resources, including majors in the B.Sc. in Natural Resources degree, potential career pathways, and post-graduate education options.

NRES 110.title: Land One: First-year Integrative Seminar
NRES 110.description: Current issues and cases in Forestry and Land and Food Systems are examined with a focus on integration of first-year subjects and exposure to both First Nations and Western perspectives.

NRES 150.title: Scholarly Writing and Argumentation in Natural Resources
NRES 150.description: Communicating concepts of forestry and links to human and environmental activities through writing, elements of argumentation, evaluating evidence, and searching for and citing references to back up claims; small-class experience. .

NRES 200.title: Forest Plant Biology I
NRES 200.description: The structure, diversity and development of trees and other plants, with emphasis on the angiosperms.

NRES 201.title: Forest Ecology
NRES 201.description: The structure and function of forest ecosystems, including: energetics; productivity; nutrient, carbon and water cycling; soils; the physical environment; population and community ecology; disturbance ecology; ecological succession; biological diversity and ecological resilience.

NRES 210.title: Forest Plant Biology II
NRES 210.description: The functional biology of trees and other forest plants in their environment, with an emphasis on gymnosperms.

NRES 211.title: Forest Classification and Silvics
NRES 211.description: Forest classification and the application of silvics in forest management, including world forest classification systems, the Biogeoclimactic Ecosystem Classification system, and ecosystem diagnosis in the field.

NRES 225.title: Communications Strategies
NRES 225.description: Strategies for thinking critically and writing effectively about topics that engage practitioners in Forestry. Planning, drafting and editing of professional-quality documents for specialists and other stakeholders. Developing oral presentation skills. .

NRES 231.title: Introduction to Biometrics
NRES 231.description: Basic theories of probability and statistics. Sampling distribution, methods of estimation and hypothesis testing; goodness of fit and tests for independence; analysis of variance, regression and correlation. Consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists:
NRES 231.corequisiteText: One of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, MATH_V 190

NRES 232.title: Computer Applications in Natural Resources
NRES 232.description: Techniques involved in solving forestry problems with microcomputers using word processing, spreadsheet, procedural language, and database management tools.

NRES 241.title: Introduction to Geomatics for Natural Resource Management
NRES 241.description: Introduction to spatial thinking and principles of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and remote sensing for natural resource management. Priority enrolment to students in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship.

NRES 341.title: Intermediate Geomatics for Natural Resource Management
NRES 341.description: Applications of remote sensing, image analysis, advanced spatial analysis and geoprocessing for natural resource management. Priority enrolment to students in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Students may receive credit for only one of NRES_V 341 or FRST_V 443. Third-year standing.

NRES 441.title: Advanced Geomatics for Natural Resource Management
NRES 441.description: Advanced applications of remote sensing, image analysis, spatial analysis and geoprocessing for natural resource management. Priority enrolment to students in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Fourth-year standing.
